g.text: 04 Temporary working state and persistent evidence memory
Two different lifetimes: LangGraph state belongs to one invocation; SQLite evidence can be reused across later related statements.
Working state | RAM, one run
Outer state: statement, start time, planning, recalled passages,
memory statistics / events, final result.
Executor state: messages[], pending_calls[], searched_filings[],
read_passage_ids[], initial_passages[], trace[], call/token counters,
format reminders, stagnant_searches, result.
Tool results and validation feedback append to messages.
There is no durable LangGraph checkpoint or resume feature.
Evidence store | SQLite, across runs
runtime/evidence_memory.sqlite | namespaced FTS5
Stored: namespace, passage_id, filing_id, source_key, quote, text.
source_key hashes canonical passage text and metadata,
including the original PDF fingerprint.
Store authenticated source material, not model verdicts.
Namespaces separate reviewer collections and benchmark modes.
Old or changed source records become recall misses.
1 Recall before verification
Remove generic date / number / unit terms.
Porter stemming + BM25 keyword candidates.
Require up to 3 topical terms to match.
Recheck fingerprint and saved quote.
Return at most 3 unique canonical passages.
2 Research the current statement
Recalled passages seed model context.
Fresh retrieval still searches all filings.
Newer disclosures can replace old facts.
Repeated search hits return IDs rather
than duplicate passage text.
3 Remember accepted sources
Only a complete result with evidence
can write to the memory namespace.
Recheck source and quote before writing.
Memory failures are traced; verification
continues with fresh corpus evidence.
What accumulates in messages[]
system: policy + tool schemas
user: claim + plan + catalogue + initial evidence
assistant: tool request → tool: source observation / error
assistant: next tool request or structured verdict submission
This transcript is resent to the model; it is not persistent memory.
Three kinds of reuse, with different purposes
Parsed-PDF cache: avoid extracting unchanged documents again.
Corpus index: fast search over canonical page passages.
Evidence memory: reuse authenticated sources across claims.
No answer cache. Memory reads/writes are measured separately
from LLM/tool calls; a hit alone is not a demonstrated saving.
Code: VerificationState in graph.py; ExecutorState in agent.py; source-key validation and recall / remember operations in memory.py.
